title: Masskara Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Masskara Marathon 2026 Review: Bacolod Heat, Field and Times
meta_description: Masskara Marathon 2026 review: Bacolod's race-morning weather, 107 marathon finishers with a 5:31 median, half and 10 km depth, and what finishers get.
dek: What the 2026 Masskara Marathon in Bacolod was like to run: how quickly the morning warmed up, how fast the marathon, half and 10 km fields finished, and what the entry covers.
verdict: Enter if you want a relaxed, low-pressure race in Bacolod with generous finishing times. The 2026 marathon had 107 finishers and a median of 5:31, and the slowest finisher took more than seven hours, so slower runners are not alone at the back. The catch is the sun. It was about 25°C and 89% humidity before dawn, then 29°C by 8am and 31°C by 10am, so the later you finish, the hotter it gets. Check the start times and pace for the heat.

sections.heading: The Race: Bacolod City, Late September
paragraphs: The 2026 race was held in Bacolod City on Sunday 27 September, with 42 km, 21 km, 10 km and 5 km races [1][2]. It is run by SMOKE10 Events Management; the 2024 edition, on 29 September 2024, was based at the Bacolod City Government Center, with routes around the centre [3].
Neither the 2026 race page nor the results gave a route map, start times or a start venue [1][2], so check those with the organiser before you book.

sections.heading: The Weather: Mild Before Dawn, Hot by Mid-Morning
paragraphs: Open-Meteo's modelled hourly weather for Bacolod on race day shows a dry, mild night: 24.9°C at 4am with a dew point of 23°C, 90% humidity and a light wind of about 5 km/h, and much the same at 5am and 6am [4].

After sunrise it warmed fast: 27.2°C at 7am, 29.2°C at 8am, 30.3°C at 9am and 31°C at 10am, with the cloud thinning to about half cover at 8am [4]. With a marathon median of 5:31 and some finishers out for more than seven hours, a large part of the marathon field was still running as the temperature climbed. Start conservatively, drink at every station and save something for the last, hottest hour.

sections.heading: Cut-offs, Entry Terms and Finisher Items
paragraphs: No cut-off times were published on the race page or with the results. The slowest recorded finishes were 7:10:47 in the marathon, 4:51:43 in the half marathon and 2:34:05 in the 10 km [1][2].

Entry fees are non-refundable and non-transferable, and runners aged 60 and over get a senior-citizen discount when registering on their own [2]. The 2024 edition gave every category a singlet, race bib, post-race snacks and a medal, with a finisher shirt for the 10 km, 21 km and 42 km; fees that year ran from ₱999 for the 5 km to ₱2,299 for the marathon [3].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The marathon had 107 finishers. The winner ran 2:52:28, almost half an hour clear of second place, and tenth place was 4:06:19. Only seven runners (7%) broke four hours and 38 (36%) broke five; the median was 5:30:51 and the 90th percentile 6:54:54. Just under a quarter of the finishers (23%) were women, the fastest in 3:44:13 [1].

The half marathon had 264 finishers, with a top ten from 1:25:07 to 1:47:26. The median was 2:47:58 and the 90th percentile 3:40:23; 20 runners (8%) broke two hours and 84 (32%) broke 2:30. Women made up 44% of the half-marathon field [1].

The 10 km was the biggest race, with 385 finishers, 56% of them women. The top ten ran between 40:00 and 46:40, but the median was 1:35:21 and only 21 runners (6%) broke an hour, so many 10 km entrants walked much of the way [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the Masskara Marathon?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want an unpressured race in Bacolod, a marathon where a five-hour finish puts you in the faster third, or a 10 km that welcomes walkers. Generous finishing times make it a reasonable first marathon for patient runners.

Think twice if you want a fast time or cool air: in 2026 the temperature passed 29°C by 8am, and the field thins out quickly behind the leaders. Ask the organiser for the route, start times and cut-offs, which were not on the 2026 race page.
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the official results and race page, an event listing for the 2024 edition and modelled historical weather.

faqs.question: How hot is the Masskara Marathon?
faqs.answer: Mild before dawn, hot by mid-morning. Modelled weather for Bacolod on 27 September 2026 gave about 25°C and 89% to 91% humidity from 4am to 6am, then 27°C at 7am, 29°C at 8am and 31°C at 10am, with no rain. Slower marathoners finish in the hottest part of the race, so pace for the heat.

faqs.question: How fast is the field at the Masskara Marathon?
faqs.answer: Mostly unhurried. In 2026, 107 runners finished the marathon, with a winning time of 2:52:28, tenth place in 4:06:19 and a median of 5:30:51; only 7% broke four hours. The half marathon had 264 finishers and a median of 2:47:58, and the 10 km median was 1:35:21.

faqs.question: What do Masskara Marathon finishers get?
faqs.answer: At the 2024 edition every category received a singlet, race bib, post-race snacks and a medal, and 10 km, 21 km and 42 km finishers also got a finisher shirt. Entry fees that year ran from ₱999 for the 5 km to ₱2,299 for the marathon. The 2026 race page did not list inclusions or fees.

editorial_notes: Reinstated 2026-11-06: official results for the 27 September 2026 edition (RaceTech PH) confirm it ran, so the review was rewritten to the template about that edition. RaceTech results list one time per runner and no clock times, so start times could not be derived; the 2026 race page gave no start times, venue, route or cut-offs. The Government Center venue, fees and inclusions are from the 2024 edition. Weather is Open-Meteo modelled hourly data for Bacolod; Bacolod-Silay airport (RPVB) is not in the Iowa Environmental Mesonet METAR archive. Runners are not named. No rating.
